questions.stem:
A manufacturer of electric generators buys engines for its generators from three companies, $R$, $S$ and $T$.

Company $R$ supplies 40% of the engines.

Company $S$ supplies 25% of the engines.

The rest of the engines are supplied by company $T$.

It is known that 2% of the engines supplied by company $R$ are faulty, 1% of the engines supplied by company $S$ are faulty and 2% of the engines supplied by company $T$ are faulty.

An engine is chosen at random.

parts.label: a
parts.text:
(a) Draw a tree diagram to show all the possible outcomes and the associated probabilities.
(2)
parts.mark_scheme:
(a) Tree diagram: first 3 branches R (0.4), S (0.25), T (0.35); second set of branches: from R, F (0.02) and F'; from S, F and F'; from T, F (0.02) and F' (0.98)
M1 A1
M1 attempt at tree with first 3 branches with R labelled 0.4 and S labelled 0.25 or second 6 branches and F labelled 0.02, 0.01 and 0.02
A1 all branches, all labels and all 9 probabilities correct
Allow equivalent fractions and percentages in all parts

parts.label: b
parts.text:

(1)
parts.mark_scheme:
(b) 0.392
B1
